v: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus,[^1] and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved friend and fellow worker,
Παῦλος δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς Φιλήμονι τῷ ἀγαπητῷ καὶ συνεργῷ ἡμῶν
and to Apphia our sister,[^2] and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house:[^3]
καὶ Ἀπφίᾳ τῇ ἀδελφῇ καὶ Ἀρχίππῳ τῷ συστρατιώτῃ ἡμῶν καὶ τῇ κατʼ οἶκόν σου ἐκκλησίᾳ·
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
I always thank my God when I mention you in my prayers,
Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου πάντοτε μνείαν σου ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου,
because I hear of your love and of the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all God's holy people,[^4]
ἀκούων σου τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ τὴν πίστιν ἣν ἔχεις πρὸς τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους,
and I pray[^5] that your sharing of the faith may become effective through the knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.[^6]
ὅπως ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου ἐνεργὴς γένηται ἐν ἐπιγνώσει παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ τοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν εἰς Χριστόν·
For I have had great joy and encouragement[^7] from your love, because the hearts[^8] of God's holy people have been refreshed through you, brother.
χαρὰν γὰρ πολλὴν ἔσχον καὶ παράκλησιν ἐπὶ τῇ ἀγάπῃ σου, ὅτι τὰ σπλάγχνα τῶν ἁγίων ἀναπέπαυται διὰ σοῦ, ἀδελφέ.
So, although in Christ I am bold enough to command you to do what is proper,
Διό, πολλὴν ἐν Χριστῷ παρρησίαν ἔχων ἐπιτάσσειν σοι τὸ ἀνῆκον,
yet for love's sake I prefer to appeal to you, being who I am, Paul, an old man,[^9] and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην μᾶλλον παρακαλῶ, τοιοῦτος ὢν ὡς Παῦλος πρεσβύτης νυνὶ δὲ καὶ δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ—
I appeal to you for my child, whom I fathered in my chains:[^10] Onesimus,[^11]
παρακαλῶ σε περὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ τέκνου, ὃν ἐγέννησα ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς Ὀνήσιμον,
who formerly was useless to you, but now is useful both to you and to me.[^12]
τόν ποτέ σοι ἄχρηστον νυνὶ δὲ σοὶ καὶ ἐμοὶ εὔχρηστον,
I am sending him back to you,[^13] him, that is, my own heart.[^14]
ὃν ἀνέπεμψά σοι αὐτόν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὰ ἐμὰ σπλάγχνα·
I would have liked to keep him with me, so that he might serve me on your behalf during my imprisonment for the good news,[^15]
ὃν ἐγὼ ἐβουλόμην πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν κατέχειν, ἵνα ὑπὲρ σοῦ μοι διακονῇ ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,
but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be done under compulsion but willingly.
χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·
For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back forever,
τάχα γὰρ διὰ τοῦτο ἐχωρίσθη πρὸς ὥραν ἵνα αἰώνιον αὐτὸν ἀπέχῃς,
no longer as a slave[^16] but more than a slave, as a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.[^17]
οὐκέτι ὡς δοῦλον ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ δοῦλον, ἀδελφὸν ἀγαπητόν, μάλιστα ἐμοί, πόσῳ δὲ μᾶλλον σοὶ καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ ἐν κυρίῳ.
So if you consider me your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
Εἰ οὖν με ἔχεις κοινωνόν, προσλαβοῦ αὐτὸν ὡς ἐμέ.
If he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
εἰ δέ τι ἠδίκησέν σε ἢ ὀφείλει, τοῦτο ἐμοὶ ἐλλόγα·
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand:[^18] I will repay it. Not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
ἐγὼ Παῦλος ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί, ἐγὼ ἀποτίσω· ἵνα μὴ λέγω σοι ὅτι καὶ σεαυτόν μοι προσοφείλεις.
Yes, brother, let me have some benefit[^19] from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.[^20]
ναί, ἀδελφέ, ἐγώ σου ὀναίμην ἐν κυρίῳ· ἀνάπαυσόν μου τὰ σπλάγχνα ἐν Χριστῷ.
Confident of your obedience, I am writing to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
πεποιθὼς τῇ ὑπακοῇ σου ἔγραψά σοι, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑπὲρ ἃ λέγω ποιήσεις.
At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be given back to you.[^21]
ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἑτοίμαζέ μοι ξενίαν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ ὅτι διὰ τῶν προσευχῶν ὑμῶν χαρισθήσομαι ὑμῖν.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
Ἀσπάζεταί σε Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my fellow workers.
Μᾶρκος, Ἀρίσταρχος, Δημᾶς, Λουκᾶς, οἱ συνεργοί μου.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.[^22]
Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν.

n.1: *Christ*: Greek *Christos*, "anointed one", the Greek equivalent of "Messiah". In Paul's letters it usually works as a name, so this translation writes "Christ". Paul's order, "Christ Jesus" or "Jesus Christ", is kept as the Greek has it.
n.3: "Your" is singular here, addressed to Philemon, and so is "you" through verse 21. In verses 3, 22 and 25 "you" is plural.
n.4: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "saints"; also in verse 7. The order of the Greek, "your love and the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the holy ones", may pair the love with God's holy people and the faith with the Lord Jesus. *Faith*: Greek *pistis* can also mean "faithfulness".
n.5: Literally "so that", continuing from "in my prayers" in verse 4.
n.6: The Greek of this verse is difficult. *Your sharing of the faith* (Greek *koinonia*, "sharing, fellowship, partnership") may mean the fellowship with others that comes from your faith, the generosity that springs from it, or your sharing of it with others. *For Christ*: or "that leads us to Christ", or "for the glory of Christ".
n.7: Many manuscripts read "For we have great thanks and encouragement".
n.8: Literally "the inward parts", the seat of the deepest feelings; also in verses 12 and 20.
n.9: Greek *presbytes*, "old man". Some interpreters take it to mean "ambassador" (*presbeutes*, a word spelled almost the same; compare Ephesians 6:20).
n.10: That is, who became a believer through Paul while Paul was in prison.
n.11: The name *Onesimus*, a common name for slaves, means "useful, beneficial". In the Greek it comes at the end of the sentence.
n.12: There is a play on the name Onesimus: once *achrestos*, "useless", now *euchrestos*, "useful". In the Greek of the time *chrestos*, "useful, good", was pronounced much like *Christos*, "Christ", and some hear a further play on that word.
n.13: Literally "I sent back", written from the point of view of the reader, who will receive the letter with Onesimus. The verb can also mean "refer to a higher authority". Many manuscripts read "I have sent him back. So receive him, that is, my own heart."
n.15: Literally "in the chains of the good news".
n.16: Greek *doulos*, "slave", also later in the verse.
n.17: That is, both in ordinary human life, as a member of your household, and as a fellow believer.
n.18: Literally "I wrote", written from the point of view of the reader; also in verse 21. Paul usually dictated his letters and wrote some words himself (compare Colossians 4:18; 2 Thessalonians 3:17).
n.19: Greek *onaimen*, "may I have benefit", from the same root as the name Onesimus.
n.22: "Your" is plural. Many manuscripts read "the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ" and add "Amen".
